environment_note: Tested in the AI-agent sandboxed browser pane. document.visibilityState remained 'hidden' throughout (pane not compositing frames in this tool), which throttles requestAnimationFrame per browser spec -- so a true rendered FPS could NOT be measured here. This is a tooling limitation, not a finding about the mesh/scene itself. Load time, parse time, and GPU-buffer-upload success/failure ARE real, measured results (these don't depend on tab visibility).
caveats: load_time_s measured over localhost (same machine) -- NOT representative of real download time over the internet for a judge-facing demo. 242.75MB over a typical demo-venue connection could take tens of seconds to minutes; this is the strongest practical argument for LOD, independent of the untested FPS question.

No crash or console error was observed for ANY variant including the un-decimated 10.67M-triangle mesh, at least through model load + GPU buffer upload -- but general WebGL/three.js practice puts a smooth-60fps budget at roughly 1-3M triangles on typical hardware, well below 10.67M, so real-time frame rate at that polycount should be assumed poor on typical hardware even though it wasn't directly measurable here.

LOD via quadric decimation is a demonstrated, working mitigation: 10.67M -> 500K triangles (21.4x reduction), 242.75MB -> 9.01MB (26.9x reduction), taking 15.5s -- fast enough to run as a one-time server-side preprocessing step, not a live-demo blocker.
